cards.front: What's the difference between continuous delivery and continuous deployment?
cards.back: Delivery keeps every passing build ready and a person releases it. Deployment releases every passing build automatically.

cards.front: Where do GitHub Actions workflows live?
cards.back: In YAML files inside `.github/workflows/`.

cards.front: What's the difference between a job and a step?
cards.back: A job is a group of steps on one runner, and jobs run in parallel unless linked with `needs`. Steps in a job run in order.

cards.front: Why use `npm ci` on CI?
cards.back: It installs exactly what the lockfile records, and fails if the lockfile doesn't match `package.json`.

cards.front: What does `npx playwright install --with-deps chromium` add to a normal install?
cards.back: It also installs the operating system libraries the browser needs.

cards.front: Should you cache Playwright browsers on CI?
cards.back: The docs advise against it. Restoring takes about as long as downloading, and the system libraries must be installed anyway.

cards.front: What does `if: ${{ !cancelled() }}` do on a step?
cards.back: Runs the step even after earlier failures, unless the run was cancelled.

cards.front: Why set `timeout-minutes` on a job?
cards.back: A stuck job would otherwise keep running until the default limit of six hours.

cards.front: What does `forbidOnly: !!process.env.CI` prevent?
cards.back: A committed `test.only` silently skipping the rest of the suite. The run fails instead.

cards.front: What exit code does a run with only flaky failures return?
cards.back: 0. Add `--fail-on-flaky-tests` to make those runs fail.

cards.front: What does the `github` reporter add?
cards.back: Failure annotations on the workflow run and on the pull request's changed files.

cards.front: Why set `reuseExistingServer: !process.env.CI`?
cards.back: CI always starts a new server, while a laptop can reuse the one already running.

cards.front: What does `--only-changed=origin/main` need on GitHub Actions?
cards.back: The Git history, so set `fetch-depth: 0` on the checkout step. The default checkout has only one commit.

cards.front: Do pull requests from forks receive repository secrets?
cards.back: No, so tests that depend on secrets can't run on those pull requests.

cards.front: What happens to a job with `needs: test` when `test` fails?
cards.back: It is skipped, unless its `if` uses a condition such as `${{ !cancelled() }}`.

cards.front: Why be careful when publishing Playwright reports on GitHub Pages?
cards.back: Pages sites are usually public, and traces can contain tokens, page content, and typed values.

cards.front: Why set `fail-fast: false` on a test matrix?
cards.back: The default cancels running jobs at the first failure, which hides whether other environments are affected.

cards.front: Why must matrix jobs use different artifact names?
cards.back: `upload-artifact@v4` fails when two jobs in a run upload the same name.

cards.front: How do you get one report from a sharded matrix?
cards.back: Use `--reporter=blob` in each job, upload the files, then run `npx playwright merge-reports` in a final job.

cards.front: What does the official Playwright Docker image include?
cards.back: Node.js, the browsers, and their system libraries. Your project's `@playwright/test` is still installed separately.

cards.front: Which version must the Playwright Docker image match?
cards.back: Your project's `@playwright/test` version. Otherwise the browsers aren't found.

cards.front: Why run Chromium containers with `--ipc=host`?
cards.back: It stops Chromium running out of shared memory and crashing.

cards.front: How does `CI` reach Playwright inside `docker run`?
cards.back: Pass it explicitly with `-e CI=true`. Containers don't inherit the host's environment.

cards.front: How do you keep the HTML report after a container exits?
cards.back: Mount the folder: `-v "$(pwd)/playwright-report:/app/playwright-report"`.
